title: Plan steward items approved during a drain together with the rest
summary: In drain_with (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs), items approved by approve_all join view.items after queue() built view.plan, so they have no plan entry and get put ahead of the plan, each alone. The fix gives each newly approved item its plan entry before planning, so approved work is ordered and batched in the plan with everything else. The audience is the operator of a parallel drain, who needs plan work to run.

defaults_applied.how: Fix where approved items miss the plan, not just one symptom.
Regression tests in the drain tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria check approved items landing in plan groups.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Root cause, from reading drain.rs: queue() builds view.plan only for items it lists. Jobs approved by approve_all in drain_with are added afterwards, so they have no entry and fall into the unplanned-first batches.
The intended fix is to plan approved items with the rest, not to change the rule for items that truly have no entry.
Approved items in a run that approves several proposals are planned with the same dependency and path-overlap rules as other items.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new drain test uses a fake Steps whose approvable proposal is approved during the drain and whose plan_entry returns an entry for the approved job. The test shows the approved job lands in a plan group (Report.plan_groups) and is not run alone ahead of the plan. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli drain.

A drain test with an approved item and several independent planned items at concurrency 2 shows the approved item batched with the plan, so planned items are worked and not starved by a failing approved item. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli drain.
cargo test and cargo clippy pass for the workspace, and cargo fmt --check is clean.

In drain_with, every item from approve_all gets a plan entry (via steps.plan_entry or equivalent) before prepare runs. An approved item whose entry cannot be built, or is incomplete, is still handled by the existing refusal path and not silently put ahead of the plan.
The comments in drain_with that say items with no plan entry go first, each alone, still describe the code accurately. Existing behavior for items that really have no plan entry is unchanged.

out_of_scope: Changing the concurrency limits or the plan grouping algorithm in athena_core::plan
Changing how steward proposals are approved or what they cost
